title: [Model loader]: support multi-thread model weight loading (#23928)

image.wheel_note: first PyPI release after merge (2025-09-13 > 2025-09-09); picked by gen_tasks.py from PyPI upload dates.
image.build: docker build -t vllm-task:23928 -f tasks/pr_23928/workload/Dockerfile --build-arg VLLM_VERSION=0.10.2 --build-arg BASE_SHA=7be141b2c52366f0cc4e731c36819aed178d2258 --build-arg MERGE_SHA=43d9ad03ba8584547537da71aee3e1810a0abbfd tasks/pr_23928/workload

workload.note: Weight-shard iteration over 8 synthetic 128 MB bf16 safetensors files (1 GB, written to a temp dir, page-cached): gold = multi_thread_safetensors_weights_iterator (8 workers), base tree lacks it so the bench runs the single-thread safetensors_weights_iterator the loader uses there. Seconds per full pass, best of 3. Author: QwQ-32B 62 GB load 20 s -> 14 s (reported-only). Opt-in feature (enable_multithread_load).

policy.one_run_is: one `docker run` of the workload cmd per arm per repeat (same image, arm tree swapped in by the prelude)

contention_gate.rules: wait while another tenant uses the GPU (>5 % util or a foreign compute process >1 GiB) or the CPU (load1 > nproc/2)

arm_isolation.tree: wipe the wheel's vllm/*.py, copy the arm's vllm/ over site-packages (compiled .so stay)
arm_isolation.files: overlay ONLY metadata.json:source_files from the arm over the wheel's own tree
arm_isolation.tests_benchmarks: copied from the PR's merge tree to /t without a sibling vllm/ package

policy.noise_model: measure.py: paired log-speedup, MAD sigma, theta = clip(k*sigma, theta_min, theta_max) with k/theta from config.yaml:measure

headline: weights_load_1gb_s

reported.experiments_note: reported = numbers from the PR body (author's machine)

author_hardware_args.text: This pull request introduces support for multi-threaded model weight loading in the `DefaultModelLoader`, allowing faster initialization of models by parallelizing the loading of safetensor and pt/bin weight files. It also adds configuratio

standalone.run_baseline: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/tasks/pr_23928:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=baseline vllm-task:23928 -lc 'A=/base; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 /task/bench.py'
standalone.run_pr_solution: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/tasks/pr_23928:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=pr_solution vllm-task:23928 -lc 'A=/gold; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 /task/bench.py'
standalone.note: The image already holds both trees (/base = baseline commit, /gold = the PR's merge commit); the one-liner swaps the chosen tree over the installed wheel exactly like run_one.sh's prelude, then runs the workload cmd from /t (the merge tree's tests/ + benchmarks/).

test_note: opt-in multi-thread loader; no test in the diff; bench writes 1 GB of synthetic shards to a temp dir and deletes them.
